_readme: The ONE file that controls what the daily job feed looks for. Edit, commit, and the next run uses it.

careers.label: Help desk / IT
careers.bench_source: BLS OOH, Computer user support specialists, May 2025 ($40,980 / $61,860 per year / 2080)

careers.label: Tech / customer support
careers.bench_source: Same as help desk (BLS computer user support specialists)

_max_entry_hourly: Jobs whose LOWEST pay is above this are almost never entry level, so the feed skips them.

local._help: Local (non-remote) jobs come from Adzuna. Keys live in GitHub Secrets. Each career uses queries_per_career searches in each place: keep the daily total low, because the free key has daily and monthly limits.

pay to train.label: Asks you to pay for training
pay to train.why: Real employers pay YOU to train. Paying upfront for 'training' is one of the most common job scams.

purchase equipment.label: Asks you to buy equipment
purchase equipment.why: Scammers send a fake check for 'equipment', you buy it from their 'vendor', the check bounces and you lose the money.

buy equipment.label: Asks you to buy equipment
buy equipment.why: Scammers send a fake check for 'equipment', you buy it from their 'vendor', the check bounces and you lose the money.

telegram.label: Interview over Telegram
telegram.why: Real companies interview by phone or video (Zoom, Teams, Google Meet). Chat-app-only interviews are a top scam sign.

whatsapp.label: Interview over WhatsApp
whatsapp.why: Real companies interview by phone or video. WhatsApp-only hiring is a common scam pattern.

signal app.label: Interview over Signal
signal app.why: Real companies interview by phone or video. Signal-only hiring is a common scam pattern.

google hangouts interview.label: Chat-only interview
google hangouts interview.why: A text-chat 'interview' lets a scammer pretend to be anyone. Real interviews include a voice or video call.

send a check.label: Check-deposit pattern
send a check.why: Fake-check scam: they send a check, ask you to deposit it and send part back. The check bounces days later and you owe the bank.

deposit a check.label: Check-deposit pattern
deposit a check.why: Fake-check scam: they send a check, ask you to deposit it and send part back. The check bounces days later and you owe the bank.

gift card.label: Gift cards mentioned
gift card.why: No real job asks you to buy or handle gift cards. Gift cards are how scammers get untraceable money.

crypto.label: Crypto payments mentioned
crypto.why: Being paid in, or asked to move, crypto is a common scam and money-laundering setup for entry-level 'jobs'.

no experience needed $.label: Big pay for no experience
no experience needed $.why: High pay with no experience and little detail is how scams hook people. Look up the company before applying.

social security number.label: Asks for SSN early
social security number.why: You only give your SSN after a real offer, on official onboarding (I-9/W-4) forms, never in an application or chat.

bank account details.label: Asks for bank details early
bank account details.why: Direct-deposit info is collected after you're hired, through HR or payroll, never before an interview.

_check_flags: Softer warnings: the job still shows, with a yellow 'check this' note explaining why.

commission only.label: Commission only
commission only.why: You're paid only when you sell. Some weeks can pay $0. Fine if you want sales, but it isn't steady hourly pay.

commission-only.label: Commission only
commission-only.why: You're paid only when you sell. Some weeks can pay $0. Fine if you want sales, but it isn't steady hourly pay.

1099.label: Contractor (1099), not employee
1099.why: No taxes are taken out, so you owe them yourself (set aside about 25-30%). Usually no benefits or overtime.

independent contractor.label: Contractor (1099), not employee
independent contractor.why: No taxes are taken out, so you owe them yourself (set aside about 25-30%). Usually no benefits or overtime.

unlimited earning.label: 'Unlimited earning potential'
unlimited earning.why: Usually means commission or MLM-style pay. Ask what a normal new hire actually earns.

be your own boss.label: 'Be your own boss'
be your own boss.why: Common wording for MLM or commission-only gigs, not a regular job.

hired immediately.label: 'Hired immediately'
hired immediately.why: Real employers interview first. Instant hiring can be a scam or a very high-turnover job.

no interview.label: No interview
no interview.why: Real employers interview first. 'No interview' hiring can be a scam or a very high-turnover job.

@gmail.com.label: Personal email to apply
@gmail.com.why: Real companies use their own email domain (name@company.com). Applying to a Gmail address is a scam sign; check the company site.

@yahoo.com.label: Personal email to apply
@yahoo.com.why: Real companies use their own email domain. Applying to a Yahoo address is a scam sign; check the company site.

@outlook.com.label: Personal email to apply
@outlook.com.why: Real companies use their own email domain. Applying to an Outlook.com address is a scam sign; check the company site.

starter kit.label: Starter kit / fee
starter kit.why: Paying for a starter kit or fee to begin work is a classic MLM or scam sign.

text us.label: Apply by text
text us.why: Real employers rarely hire through text messages. Look up the company and apply on its own site.

reshipping.label: Reshipping
reshipping.why: 'Receive and reship packages' jobs are package-mule scams; you can end up shipping stolen goods.

package handling from home.label: Reshipping
package handling from home.why: 'Receive and reship packages' jobs are package-mule scams; you can end up shipping stolen goods.

_sources: Turn a job site off by setting it to false.

themuse._help: Entry-level jobs from The Muse near these places (plus remote). Free, no key.

_remote_search: remote_search: false = these jobs are mostly in-person, so don't ask the remote-only sites (Himalayas) about them. Local sources (The Muse, Adzuna) still find them.
